docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Welcome to CloudBridge! Multiple clouds, one Kotlin Multiplatform bridge. Supporting Android, iOS, web and desktop (JVM).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The library is published to Maven Central.

dependencies {
    implementation("nl.jacobras:cloudbridge:0.10.0")
}

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
In general, CloudBridge works as follows:

// 1: Instantiate a service
val service = CloudBridge.dropbox()

// 2: Authenticate (platform- and service-specific, see docs)
service.authenticate("clientId", "example://redirect-uri")

// 3: Ready for use!
service.listFiles("/".asFolderPath())

See Cloud services on how to authenticate each service on every platform.

See shared API for all available operations.

See the demo app source for more example code.

Warning

The library doesn't refresh tokens yet, so once a token expires you'll need to re-authenticate. Follow https://github.com/jacobras/CloudBridge/issues/25 for updates.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text: CloudBridge aims to make it easy to support multiple cloud services in your app, without having to go learn every detail of each specific service.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: The library only supports limited/private app folders, no full access.

docs.title: Paths and IDs
docs.text: The library prefers to work with IDs over paths.

docs.title: Strongly typed
docs.text: id and path variables are typed as much as possible, to prevent accidental mix-ups.

docs.title: Unified error handling
docs.text:
Dropbox will throw 409 when it can't find a path. Other services throw 404. CloudBridge turns them both into CloudServiceException.NotFoundException. The same for all other errors, see Errors for an overview.

Feel free to open an issue if you have a different use case for any of these.

docs.title: Checking authentication
docs.text:
val service = CloudBridge.dropbox(token)

if (service.isAuthenticated()) {
    // Ready to use.
}

Call setToken() to attach or replace the access token used for authentication, for example after loading a previously stored token:

service.setToken(storedToken)

docs.title: Getting user info
docs.text:
try {
    val userInfo = service.getUserInfo()
    println(userInfo.name)
    println(userInfo.emailAddress)
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: All suspending calls can throw a CloudServiceException.

docs.title: Common exceptions
docs.text:
These are expected in normal use.

Exception Cause CloudServiceException.ConflictException An item with the same name already exists CloudServiceException.ConnectionException A network error occurred CloudServiceException.InsufficientSpaceException The account has no storage space left CloudServiceException.NotAuthenticatedException The service has no valid access token (yet) CloudServiceException.NotFoundException The requested item could not be found

docs.title: Less common exceptions
docs.text:
These are not expected to happen during normal use.

Exception Cause CloudServiceException.IllegalArgumentException An argument is invalid, e.g. a missing or wrong sizeInBytes for a large OneDrive upload CloudServiceException.SinkWriteException Writing the download to the Sink failed CloudServiceException.SourceReadException Reading the Source to upload failed CloudServiceException.Unknown Any other unexpected error

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Files and folders are addressed with FilePath and FolderPath, both of which always start with a slash. Create them with the asFilePath() / asFolderPath() extension functions:

val file = "/Projects/welcome.txt".asFilePath()
val folder = "/Projects".asFolderPath()
val root = "/".asFolderPath()

docs.title: Listing files
docs.text:
Lists all files and folders one level deep; nested content is not fetched.

try {
    val items = service.listFiles("/".asFolderPath())
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Listing delta changes
docs.text:
Lists all file/folder changes since the last time this was called. Not supported by all services, see Cloud services for the support matrix.

try {
    val result = service.getDelta(previousCursor)
    val previouCursor = result.newCursor
    val changes = result.changes
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Getting file or folder info
docs.text:
Fetches the metadata of a single file or folder. If nothing exists at the path, or the item has the other type (a folder when asking for a file or the other way round), a NotFoundException is thrown.

try {
    val file: CloudFile = service.getFileInfo("/Projects/Welcome.txt".asFilePath())
    val folder: CloudFolder = service.getFolderInfo("/Projects".asFolderPath())
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

Calling getFolderInfo() for the root folder (/) throws an IllegalArgumentException.

docs.title: Creating a folder
docs.text:
try {
    service.createFolder("/Projects".asFolderPath())
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Creating a text file
docs.text:
try {
    val file: CloudFile = service.createFile("/Projects/Welcome.txt".asFilePath(), "Hello world!")
    println("Created ${file.id} at revision ${file.revision}")
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Updating a text file
docs.text:
try {
    val file: CloudFile = service.updateFile(fileId, "Updated content")
    println("Updated ${file.id} to revision ${file.revision}")
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Uploading binary or large files
docs.text:
For images, archives and other binary content, pass a kotlinx.io.Source. The content is read until its end, but the stream isn't closed. Files larger than 10 MB are automatically uploaded in chunks1.

try {
    val localPath = Path("photo.jpg")
    SystemFileSystem.source(localPath).buffered().use { source ->
        service.createFile(
            path = localPath.name.asFilePath(),
            source = source,
            sizeInBytes = SystemFileSystem.metadataOrNull(localPath)?.size,
            mimeType = "image/jpeg"
        )
    }
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}
  • sizeInBytes is optional, except for OneDrive files larger than 10 MB (throws a CloudServiceException.IllegalArgumentException if missing or not matching the content size in that case).
  • mimeType defaults to application/octet-stream. Dropbox doesn't store MIME types and ignores it.
  • WebDAV has no chunked uploads, so the content is streamed in a single request.
  • updateFile() has as similar signature as createFile().

docs.title: Using an InputStream
docs.text:
Here's an example on how to use an InputStream on Android and desktop:

try {
    val file = File("photo.jpg")
    file.inputStream().use { stream ->
        service.createFile(
            path = file.name.asFilePath(),
            source = stream.asSource().buffered(),
            sizeInBytes = file.length(),
            mimeType = "image/jpeg"
        )
    }
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Downloading a file
docs.text:
try {
    val content: String = service.downloadFile(fileId)
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

docs.title: Downloading binary or large files
docs.text:
For images, archives and other binary content, pass a kotlinx.io.Sink. The content is streamed into it, so large files aren't held in memory. The sink is flushed, but not closed.

try {
    SystemFileSystem.sink(Path("photo.jpg")).buffered().use { sink ->
        service.downloadFile(fileId, sink)
    }
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

To get the content in memory instead, use a Buffer:

val buffer = Buffer()
service.downloadFile(fileId, buffer)
val bytes = buffer.readByteArray()

docs.title: Moving or renaming a file or folder
docs.text:
To rename an item, move it within the same folder. If an item already exists at the new path, a CloudServiceException.ConflictException is thrown.

try {
    // Rename/move a file
    service.moveFile(fileId, "/Projects/New name.txt".asFilePath())

    // Or a folder
    service.moveFolder(folderId, "/Projects2".asFolderPath())
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

On WebDAV, the id of an item is its path, so the returned item has a new id.

docs.title: Deleting a file or folder
docs.text:
try {
    service.delete(itemId)
} catch (e: CloudServiceException) {
    // Handle...
}

  1. Chunk size is around 10 MB, which is "optimal for stable high speed connections" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-createuploadsession?view=graph-rest-1.0#best-practices). See the support matrix for details. ↩

docs.title: API
docs.text:
First, authenticate the service you wish to use (see Services). Once authenticated, every service exposes the same shared API described in this section.

There may be differences, see Cloud services for the support matrix.

docs.title: ☁️ Dropbox
docs.text:
Start by instantiating the service:

val service = CloudBridge.dropbox()

Then, authenticate using the platform-specific methods below. Once authenticated, the shared API is available.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Path case insensitivity

Dropbox paths are case-insensitive, meaning /Folder/File.txt and /folder/file.txt refer to the same file.

docs.title: Registration in App Console
docs.text:
Info

Your app needs to be registered in the Dropbox App Console.

Make sure to register the redirect URIs there:

docs.title: Authenticating
☁️ Google Drive
docs.text:
Start by instantiating the service:

val service = CloudBridge.googleDrive()

Then, authenticate using the platform-specific methods below. Once authenticated, the shared API is available.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
App Data folder visibilityDuplicationFile typesPaths

The App Data folder is not shown to users. A user can only see the amount of space it takes up by going to drive.google.com and navigating to Settings » Manage apps.

Files and folders don't need unique names in Google Drive. To avoid confusing duplicates, CloudBridge does its best to prevent them: createFile(), createFolder(), moveFile() and moveFolder() first check the target folder and throw a ConflictException if a file/folder with the new name already exists.

Folders in Google Drive are just files, but with the mimetype application/vnd.google-apps.folder.

Google Drive doesn't have the concept of paths. Instead, every file has a list of "parent file IDs". In the past, there could be multiple, but now every file can have just one parent.

To offer a unified API, CloudBridge still builds a path for Drive files. It will contain the parent file ID and filename. For example, a nested folder could look like /A2vXis2oKtcHO/9xZDTanHiFcgg/ and a file inside a folder could be /9xZDTanHiFcgg/promotion.txt.

Passing in a deeper path on a file (for example /id1/id2/file.txt) has no effect, as only the last part (id2) is set as a parent to the file/folder.

When retrieving changes with getDelta(), Google Drive only reports the ID of deleted items. The path of a DeletedDeltaChange is therefore /<fileId>, so match deletions on itemId.

docs.title: Registration in Cloud Console
docs.text:
Info

Every platform needs to be registered in the Google Cloud Console as "OAuth 2.0 Client ID" with the correct type (e.g., iOS, Android, Web, Desktop).

docs.title: Authenticating
☁️ OneDrive
docs.text:
Start by instantiating the service:

val service = CloudBridge.oneDrive()

Then, authenticate using the platform-specific methods below. Once authenticated, the shared API is available.

docs.title: Registration in App Console
docs.text:
Info

Your app needs to be registered in the Microsoft Azure Portal.

Make sure to register the redirect URIs there:

For web, choose Single-page application as the platform.

docs.title: Authenticating
Cloud services
docs.text:
These subpages show how to authenticate on each platform, and any remarks/limitations of specific services.

Service Data in app folder Support Delta support Chunk size Dropbox 👁️ Visible to users ✔️ All platforms ✅ Yes 8 MB 4 Google Drive 📦 Not visible to users1 ✔️ All platforms ✅ Yes 10 MB 5 OneDrive 👁️ Visible to users ✔️ All platforms ✅ Yes 10 MB 6 WebDAV 👁️ Visible to users ✔️ All platforms2 ❌ No3 Not chunked
  • "All platforms" means Android, iOS, desktop (JVM) and web (JS/WASM).
  • "Chunk size" is the size of each part in which files larger than 10 MB are uploaded.

  1. "App data not visible" means the user will not see the app files when opening the cloud folder themselves (e.g. on user's desktop or in the web interface of Google Drive). More details. ↩

  2. WebDAV on web requires dealing with CORS. Some providers, like Fastmail, block requests from all domains. ↩

  3. You could keep the last result of a call and compare a new result manually to get delta support with WebDAV. ↩

  4. A multiple of 4 MB, as required by Dropbox. ↩

  5. A multiple of 256 KB, as required by Google Drive. ↩

  6. A multiple of 320 KB, as required by OneDrive. ↩

docs.title: ☁️ WebDAV
docs.text:
Start by instantiating the service:

val service = CloudBridge.webDav(
    WebDavCredentials(
        serverUrl = "https://example.com/webdav",
        username = "your-username",
        password = "your-password"
    )
)

Then the shared API is available.

docs.title: Android
docs.text:
Set up a deeplink filter inside AndroidManifest.xml:

<!-- OAuth redirect deep link: com.example.myapp://cloudbridge-auth -->
<intent-filter>
    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
    <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
    <data android:scheme="com.example.myapp" android:host="cloudbridge-auth" />
</intent-filter>

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. The recommended format for CloudBridge is com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth, where com.example.app matches your app's identifier, but there's no hard requirement for this structure.

Open the auth URL in a Custom Tab and capture the redirect. Then exchange the authorization code for a token:

// When user wants to authenticate:
val url = service.authenticate(
    clientId = "yourClientId",
    redirectUri = "yourRedirectUri" // e.g. a custom scheme like "com.example://cloudbridge-auth"
)
CustomTabsIntent.Builder().build().launchUrl(context, url.toUri())

// In your Activity's onNewIntent (and onCreate), call:
val uri = intent.data ?: return
val token = service.completeAuthentication(
    clientId = "yourClientId",
    redirectUri = "com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth", // Needs to match the uri passed into authenticate()
    intentUri = uri
)

Securely store the token and pass it to the constructor of the service to use it.

docs.title: Desktop
docs.text:
val authServer = LocalAuthenticationServer() // optional parameter: `port=8080`

// Build auth URL and open it in the browser
val url = service.authenticate(
    authServer = authServer,
    clientId = "yourClientId",
    onSuccess = { token ->
        service.setToken(token)
        TODO("Store the token locally")
    }
)
openBrowser(url)

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. Since CloudBridge on desktop uses a loopback server, the URL will be http://localhost:8080 (or whichever port you specify).

docs.title: iOS
docs.text:
service.authenticate(
    clientId = "yourClientId",
    redirectUri = "com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth" // change to your app
)?.let { token ->
    service.setToken(token)
    TODO("Store the token locally")
}

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. The recommended format for CloudBridge is com.example.app://cloudbridge-auth, where com.example.app matches your app's identifier, but there's no hard requirement for this structure.

docs.title: Web
docs.text:
// Always call this:
val token = service.completeAuthentication()
if (token != null) {
    service.setToken(token)
}

// When user wants to authenticate:
val uri = service.authenticate(
    clientId = "yourClientId",
    redirectUri = "yourRedirectUri"
)
window.location.href = uri

The redirect URL needs to be configured in the service's API console. For example, https://example.com/cloudbridge-callback, where https://example.com matches your app's domain, but there's no hard requirement for this structure.
